summary: An excerpt from the fiction 'Book 10 — part 105' showing a tense standoff in a fog-bound forest between surveyors and the narrator Lee-Daniel, with investors (the Series A and Series B men) watching via a tablet. A surveyor wrecks the bus skylight and then flees with stolen office supplies, prompting remarks that such people are not truly fired. Lee-Daniel and Elaine, tied off in trees, are under laser sights and gunfire from Cobra's rifle, and he tells Elaine to push the surveyors off the branches. The Series B investor warns Lee-Daniel to stop advising them so he is not liable.
one_line: In a foggy standoff, Lee-Daniel and Elaine are pinned in trees by gunfire while investors on a tablet pressure him over surveyors who are fleeing or falling.
key_facts: Lee-Daniel speaks in the grudging half-sentences that Cobra had preferred, a manner that makes him feel crazy, brave and alien.
A surveyor broke through the bus's safety-glass skylight and dropped inside, where a headlamp beam jumped around the interior.
Lee-Daniel knew the surveyor in the bus snored, did tricks with a butterfly knife, and sent money home to his little sister in Muncie.
The surveyor who crawled out of the sunroof carried a pillowcase stuffed with schwag and ran down the freeway shoulder toward Buffalo.
Lee-Daniel says the investors are spear-carriers, fronts for unimaginable, implacable wealth, charged with returning 400 percent over three years on a national-budget-sized fund.
Lee-Daniel tells Elaine to get down, saying 'They can't see us,' while laser sights dance in the fog.
Elaine is wedged into a crook and tied off with an improvised harness of nylon rope and carabiners from her vest.
Lee-Daniel hears the crack of Cobra's rifle, and Elaine says, 'He's scared.'
A young surveyor with a shaved head, picked up in Montana, is wrapped around a branch, locked at the ankles, thighs and wrists.
Lee-Daniel tells Elaine, 'Get him down. Push him off the branch if you have to.'
A balding forty-something surveyor with a comb-over hangs on the trunk of the branch below Elaine, and Lee-Daniel says, 'Push him too.'
The Series B man speaks from the tablet stuck in Lee-Daniel's waistband, telling him, 'Don't give them any more advice.'
The Series B man says Lee-Daniel should not be liable for what the surveyors do in this situation.
